headline_marked: Qualcomm Snapdragon C: [[67% faster battery]] than Intel N250 for $300 laptops
headline: Qualcomm Snapdragon C: 67% faster battery than Intel N250 for $300 laptops
summary: The new ARM-based chip boasts significant battery efficiency gains and faster performance on battery power, aiming to compete in the budget laptop market.
details: Qualcomm has detailed its upcoming Snapdragon C chip, an 8-core ARM-based processor designed for laptops around the $300 price point. The chip features a single-core max frequency of 3 GHz and a multi-core max of 2 GHz, with an integrated Adreno GPU and Hexagon NPU.

In performance tests pitting a Snapdragon C reference design against an Intel N250-powered Acer TravelMate, Qualcomm claims up to 67% better battery performance and 2.1 times greater battery efficiency.

On battery power, the Snapdragon C showed up to 44% faster single-threaded and 24% faster multi-core performance in Geekbench, and significant gains in Cinebench. However, Qualcomm did not publish benchmarks for when the systems are plugged in.

Qualcomm also highlighted battery efficiency improvements in specific tasks, reporting 106% better performance for Netflix, 68% for web browsing, and 74% for Teams video calls compared to the Intel N250.

Several OEMs, including HP, Acer, Asus, and Lenovo, are expected to release Snapdragon C-powered laptops. Acer has already shown a prototype of its Aspire Go 15, but release dates and final pricing are still unconfirmed.

While Qualcomm guides for a $300 price point, the actual cost of components, particularly memory, could impact this. The launch timing might align with the IFA trade show, or partners may wait until CES.
